_canonical: This is the ONE canonical Wave 1 tracking file (crush_feat_plan.md, 'Progress tracking'). feat-wave-W1-progress.json was a duplicate created by a drifting naming convention and has been deleted. Status here is derived from git log + a real full-suite run, never from an agent's self-report.
afterWave1Partial: Tests: 3614, Assertions: 9328, Warnings: 11, Skipped: 1. (0 failures, 0 errors)
runNotes: Run 1 (claude-code Workflow, 66 agents) attempted 16 of 27 steps; tracks halt at their first block, so 10 steps were never attempted.

Design flaw in run 1: no commit between steps, so all 16 steps' work accumulated in one working tree and every reviewer flagged 'cannot isolate this step' as a traceability finding. Several BLOCKED verdicts are that artifact, not a code defect.

Plan flaw surfaced by run 1: category 11 (Production Reachability) is a mandatory blocker, but Wave 1 file lists exclude Chat.php/Renderer.php/Bootstrap.php where production wiring lives. For any step whose spec says 'surface X to the user' the two rules are mutually unsatisfiable. Builders resolved it by following crush_feat.md (the spec) over crush_feat_plan.md (the decomposition).

Three genuine code defects found by reviewers were fixed before commit: ForeignSkillDiscovery precedence backwards vs its own test name and SkillLoader's documented convention; Edit's diff concatenated into content instead of a ToolResult field, plus a false-success return when old_string was absent; ReasoningExtractor's !empty() treating a literal '0' as absent.

Run 3 (worktrees): 3 tracks concurrent, each in its own git worktree on its own branch, committing per step. Zero cross-track contamination and all three merged into master with no conflicts -- the file-disjointness analysis held. Track A completed all 4 steps clean.

Harness flaw in run 3: any FINDINGS verdict counted as non-PASS, so W1.B3a blocked after 3 cycles despite ZERO blocking findings (all low/info) and a green suite -- a step that only accumulates nits can never converge. Both blocked steps' real defects were fixed by hand and committed. A future run should let a reviewer PASS with recorded minor findings.

W1.A2.note: Reviewer verdict was BLOCKED purely on shared-tree traceability + scope (Renderer/Message/EngineBackend outside the manifest row). Kept: §12 D3's spec explicitly requires the TUI half the plan row omitted. Its low-severity empty('0') finding was fixed.

W1.B2b.note: Disclosed gap kept honestly: only loadForPath()'s expansion has a live production call path. loadRoot() gets its caller in W1.B3a, which was never attempted this run.

W1.B3a.note: Reviewer returned BLOCKED after 3 cycles but found no blocker -- all findings low/info. Fixed by hand: root AGENTS.md was injected twice on any repo whose CLAUDE.md @-imports it (this repo exactly), wasting context every turn; deduplicated via a realpath-keyed emitted-set in InstructionFileLoader. Also added the missing empty-document-guard test.

W1.C2.note: Builder self-amended its own row in crush_feat_plan.md to widen scope to SkillRegistry.php. Amendment kept -- registerFromManifest() hardcoded paths: [], silently breaking path-based auto-scoping -- but flagged: an agent editing the plan to justify its own scope is exactly the drift Lesson 1/2 warn about.

W1.D2a.note: Reviewer's category-11 blocker is correct but premature: ForeignSkillDiscovery's production wiring is W3.S8 (AppBuilder), not a Wave 1 step. Its real finding -- backwards project/home precedence -- was fixed.

W1.D2b.note: Reviewer returned BLOCKED with one genuine medium finding: opencode tools: map read as $enabled ? allow : deny, so any truthy non-boolean silently GRANTED tool access. Fixed to fail closed. Also fixed list-form tools: importing array indices as tool names, and a 2-way ternary dispatching a 4-case enum.

W1.E2.note: Both findings were low severity (a stale line-number citation and an untested default-parameter branch).

W1.E3.note: Never dispatched as its own step -- W1.E2's builder wired bin/sugarcrush as part of its work. Verified present in the diff: --help and -p now dispatch before Program/Bootstrap::chat(), fixing the blocking-TUI bug.

W1.F1.note: Both real findings fixed: diff moved onto a ToolResult field; no-op edit now returns an honest error instead of false success. Two tests that locked in the false success were re-pointed at the contract.

W1.G2.note: Reviewer's dead-code blocker was real and is resolved -- but by a fix agent inventing a Doctor built-in tool to manufacture a call path. Kept because §9 E4 specs /doctor and §9's own PR sequencing puts it with E1+E2. Two genuine bugs fixed en route: base64 across the fork/JSON IPC seam, and ToolResult passthrough instead of ok() re-wrapping.
